Date: 10/29/2026 | Staff: Daisy | Type: Phone consultation, reentry navigation
Outcome: He lives in Sumter County, which is outside our service area, so he’s starting with reentry navigation. He’s very interested in First Shift in Columbia. The plan is to find him housing in Columbia first, then add him to the Columbia waitlist. His top two priorities are housing and getting his license reinstated.

Housing

Living with his mother. He’s not happy staying there long-term.
Gets denied almost everywhere he applies. He has no evictions and believes it’s because of his record.
Open to transitional or shared housing.
Wants to live on the Garners Ferry side of Columbia so he can still drop his son at school.
Income for rent: DoorDash plus occasional side clients. Earns about $700–$1,000 every two weeks.

Documents

Birth certificate: Yes
Social Security card: No physical card. He has a copy on his phone and knows his number.
State ID: Yes
Driver’s license: Suspended (second suspension in a row) with over $2,000 in tickets. The DMV told him the suspension was over and he only needed to pay the tickets, but it showed as still suspended when he was stopped. He thinks he may be near the 2-year point where reinstatement opens up but isn’t sure.

Transportation

Family members drive him when needed.
He said he’d drive his own car to the program (see To verify, since his license is suspended).

Availability

Takes his son to school, with drop-off by 8 AM. He thinks he could reach a Columbia center around 9, depending on where he lives. No other weekday conflicts mentioned.

Health / Substance Use

No prescribed medications in the last 5 years.
No emergency needs (medical, mental health, housing, or prescriptions).
No history of major alcohol abuse.
No drug use other than marijuana that he considers “worth mentioning.” He said he “might have tried something once.”
Told him about weekly drug testing, including marijuana. He said he isn’t currently using.
Legally and physically able to work.

Justice Involvement

Age at first arrest: about 17 (a school fight)
Total arrests: about 10
Convictions: pleaded guilty to 2 charges at the same time. He says the rest were pending or thrown out.
Incarcerations: about 10 (first pass only, see To verify)
Most recent release: last Friday (10/23) from jail, after a few days. He said he was locked up about a week ago and it cost him a job (see To verify).
Most recent conviction included drug trafficking or firearm possession: No
Biological parents’ criminal record: No
Probation or parole: unclear, see To verify.
Pending charges: state, in Sumter County. Driving under suspension plus an added count tied to a DUI from some years ago (habitual or DUI offender). He was clear it’s not a new DUI.

Child Support

Court-ordered and he pays. He’s not sure whether he’s in arrears and thinks he may owe around $4,000.

Education / Employment

Highest education: some college
Work history: quality inspection, material handling, forklift operation
Longest job: about 3 years
Jobs usually ended because an assignment ended, he was fired, or he quit for a better opportunity. Not because of incarceration.
Certifications: OSHA 10. Forklift certified once about 10 years ago (probably expired). Some kind of HVAC certification. A light industrial technical certification.

Program Info Given

Reentry navigation: phone-based help with resources, license reinstatement funding, resumes, and job leads.
First Shift (Columbia): 8 weeks, Monday through Friday, 9–3. $450 a week stipend based on points (minus $9 for each lost point). Morning class, forklift certification, SkillCat trade courses, and a weekly case manager meeting. Job placement at the end.
There’s currently a waitlist. Told him the drug test only looks back about 2 weeks.

Next Steps

Daisy: Look into Columbia housing partners with vacancies or open beds, ideally near Garners Ferry. Follow up later today or tomorrow.
Zerrick: Go to the DMV today or tomorrow morning, get a printout of his reinstatement requirements, and send Daisy a photo.
Daisy: Once the printout comes in, check whether he’s eligible for reinstatement funding.
Later: Add him to the Columbia waitlist once his housing is set. | [Update 10/26/2026 • Daisy Boynton]: No answer
